paper_title: Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models
caption: Random (light color) and random (darker color) performance comparison with different perturbation setups and the unperturbed trained model variants (orange bars). Left-to-right: Blue: Accuracy of the embedding and first layers' probes; Green: Random models with pre-trained embedding layer: no perturbation, , , , ; Red: Random models where the embedding layer is random as well: no perturbation, , , , ; Orange: Unperturbed trained models.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the accuracy of various model configurations under different perturbation setups, comparing random models with and without pre-trained embeddings to unperturbed trained models. The vertical axis represents accuracy, ranging from 70 to 95 in increments of 5, while the horizontal axis lists the model configurations in a left-to-right sequence: "embedding", "1st layer", "random layers", "random layers +B2", "random layers +L2", "random layers +R2", "random layers +permute", "random", "random +B2", "random +L2", "random +R2", "random +permute", and "unperturbed". Each configuration has one or two bars, with lighter and darker shades indicating different conditions. The blue bars (light and dark) correspond to probes of the embedding and first layers, with the dark blue bar generally slightly higher than the light blue one, both hovering around 80–82 accuracy. The green bars represent random models with pre-trained embedding layers; the light green bars are consistently around 79–80 accuracy, while the dark green bars are slightly higher, around 81–82 accuracy, across all perturbation types (no perturbation, +B2, +L2, +R2, +permute). The red bars represent random models with random embedding layers; the light red bars are consistently around 72 accuracy, and the dark red bars are around 73–74 accuracy, indicating minimal improvement from perturbations. The orange bars, representing the unperturbed trained models, show the highest accuracy, with the light orange bar at approximately 90 and the dark orange bar at approximately 92, clearly outperforming all other configurations. The bars are grouped by configuration, with no explicit stacking, and are arranged in a fixed order along the x-axis, with no sorting by value. The chart visually emphasizes the significant performance gap between unperturbed trained models and all random variants.
